# Natasha / Daniel
Date: 2026-09-07 | Duration: 54.709999084472656m

## Summary
The session explained how to configure GitHub access with SSH, including generating a key with ssh-keygen, setting private-key permissions with chmod 600, adding the key to the SSH agent, and resolving an access-confirmation issue through a password reset and screen sharing. The main repository was forked to a personal GitHub account, cloned through its SSH URL, and recloned after deleting the local folder to restore a clean copy. A descriptive local branch was created for a documentation fix. Patch files were discussed with git apply and git am, with Daniel preferring manual patch management. The workflow for pushing a branch to a personal fork and opening a pull request was demonstrated. GitHub pull requests can be used to review file differences, request engineer approval, and wait for automated tests before merging. Natasha will attempt a small bug fix independently using the documented process, and Daniel will share the current recording for review and future learning.

## Keywords
Git, SSH key, GitHub fork, branch management, AI documentation patching, pull request workflow
